title: Supply and inventory
hired_for: To keep best sellers in stock without tying cash up in slow stock, know what each unit really costs to land, and get every parcel delivered the first time.

jobs.job: Never run out of a best seller
jobs.why: A stockout on a top product stops sales, wastes the ads pointing at it and sends buyers to a rival who may keep them.

watch.metric: stockout days on the top 20 products by gross profit, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS)

drives.metric: sales lost to stockouts (proxy: average daily sales times stockout days)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 top products were out for 11 days last month, about $38,000 in lost sales. After: reorders placed on time, 0 stockout days next month.

jobs.job: Order the right amount at the right time
jobs.why: Ordering by gut means too much of slow items and too little of fast ones. A reorder point per product, from sales speed and supplier lead time, fixes both.

watch.metric: products below their reorder point with no open purchase order, weekly
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS) and supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 7 products below reorder point with no order placed. After: a weekly review keeps it at 0.

jobs.job: Stop ads and promos on products about to run out
jobs.why: Spending to sell a product that will be gone in a week buys angry customers and back orders. Pausing or shifting spend protects both.

watch.metric: ad spend on products with under 14 days of stock left, weekly
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads, joined to Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,200 last week on ads for a product with 6 days of stock. After: spend moved to products with 60 days of stock.

jobs.job: Know what each product really costs to land
jobs.why: The factory price is not the cost. Freight, duty, tariffs and exchange rates can add 20% to 40%, and margins set on the old number are wrong.

watch.metric: landed cost per unit versus the cost used in the margin plan, per purchase order
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain and Shopify product cost field

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: margin plan uses $3.10 per pair, true landed cost is $3.85 after a new tariff. After: prices and promos reset on $3.85.

jobs.job: Be ready for the peak season
jobs.why: Q4 and Black Friday can be a third of the year's sales. Stock that lands late, or a warehouse without staff, loses the best weeks.

watch.metric: top products with stock on hand versus the peak target, and share of peak orders landed by the cut-off date
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS) and supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

drives.metric: stockout days in the peak weeks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 60% of peak stock is due to land after 1 November. After: orders moved up 3 weeks, 95% lands by 15 October.

jobs.job: Cut failed deliveries and parcels sent back
jobs.why: A failed delivery means paying to ship twice or refunding, plus a worried customer. Some carriers and regions fail far more than others.

watch.metric: first-attempt delivery rate and return-to-sender rate by carrier and region, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify fulfilment events and the shipping app (ShipStation, AfterShip)

drives.metric: shipping and refund cost per order

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4% of parcels go back to sender in 2 rural regions. After: address checks and a better carrier there bring it to 1.5%.

jobs.job: Work today's delivery problems before the parcel goes back
jobs.why: A wrong address or missed delivery has a short window to fix. Miss it and the parcel returns, costing 2 shipping legs.

watch.metric: open delivery exceptions with under 24 hours left to act, daily
watch.source: Shopify fulfilment events and the shipping app (ShipStation, AfterShip)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 35 open exceptions, 12 close today. After: a daily queue gets each one a call or text, 3 end up returned.

jobs.job: Free cash stuck in slow and dead stock
jobs.why: Stock that does not sell is cash you cannot spend on ads or new product. It also costs storage every month.

watch.metric: value of stock with no sale in 180 days, at landed cost, monthly
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $62,000 in stock unsold for 180 days. After: bundles and a clearance sale free $40,000 in 60 days.

jobs.job: Hold the warehouse to the dispatch times it promised
jobs.why: Late dispatch shows up as late parcels, status tickets and refunds, even when the carrier did its job.

watch.metric: share of orders shipped within the promised dispatch time, weekly
watch.source: 3PL or warehouse dispatch log and Shopify fulfilment events and the shipping app (ShipStation, AfterShip)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 82% of orders ship in 1 business day. After: a service credit clause and weekly review lift it to 97%.

jobs.job: Order stock ahead of launches, promos and ad pushes
jobs.why: Past sales do not predict a planned push. A big promo on stock sized for a normal month sells out in days.

watch.metric: stock on hand versus planned units for products in upcoming promos, weekly
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS) and the promo calendar in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the spring sale plans 8,000 units with 3,000 in stock. After: a demand plan and early order cover 100%.

jobs.job: See store and marketplace stock in one place
jobs.why: Stock split across the warehouse and Amazon can starve one channel while the other sits full. Running out on Amazon hurts ranking for weeks.

watch.metric: stock cover in days per product by channel (store warehouse, Amazon FBA)
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS) and Amazon Seller Central

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: FBA out on 2 top products while the home warehouse has 90 days. After: weekly transfers keep FBA above 30 days.

jobs.job: Pick the right carrier for each region
jobs.why: Carriers differ by region on price, speed and failure rate. One default carrier often overpays and underdelivers.

watch.metric: cost per delivered parcel and on-time share by carrier and region, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify fulfilment events and the shipping app (ShipStation, AfterShip) and carrier invoices

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: one carrier everywhere, $8.40 per parcel. After: split by region, $7.60 with on-time share up 4 points.

jobs.job: Catch defects before they reach customers
jobs.why: A bad batch that ships becomes refunds, returns and bad reviews. An inspection before the goods leave the factory is cheaper than any of those.

watch.metric: defect rate found at receiving, per purchase order, and returns tagged 'defective', 60 day
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain and Shopify return reasons

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no inspection, 3% of units returned as defective. After: inspection before final payment, under 1%.

jobs.job: Renew supplier prices before the deal runs out
jobs.why: When a price lock ends without notice, the next order can cost more and margin drops before anyone sees it.

watch.metric: supplier contracts ending in 60 days with no renewal started
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

drives.metric: cost per unit on the next order

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 contracts end next month, not raised. After: both renewed at the old price for 12 months.

jobs.job: Collect every cash-on-delivery payment the courier owes (cash on delivery markets only)
jobs.why: In markets that use cash on delivery, couriers pay the brand later. Short payments add up unless each order is checked. Reads null for a US brand.

watch.metric: expected cash-on-delivery amount minus amount paid by the courier, weekly
watch.source: courier payment reports joined to Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3% of cash-on-delivery value is unaccounted for. After: weekly matching and disputes bring it under 0.3%.

jobs.job: Do not depend on one supplier or one country
jobs.why: If one factory or one country makes most of the stock, one fire, strike or tariff stops sales for months.

watch.metric: largest supplier's share of units bought, 12 month, and top products with a vetted backup factory
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

drives.metric: stockout days after a supply shock

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 85% of units from one factory, no backup. After: a second factory approved for the top 3 products.

jobs.job: Score suppliers on time, defects and price
jobs.why: Suppliers slip slowly. A running score shows who is getting worse before a late or bad order causes a stockout.

watch.metric: supplier on-time delivery and defect rate per purchase order, rolling 90 day
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no record of late orders. After: one supplier shows 3 late orders in a row and gets a backup.

jobs.job: Lower the unit cost of long-running products
jobs.why: Mature products often keep the price agreed at launch. A cost-down backed by real part costs and a second quote can add points of margin on every unit.

watch.metric: cost per unit on top products versus the last agreed price, per purchase order
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: hero product cost unchanged for 3 years at $3.20. After: a second quote and a volume tier bring it to $2.95.

jobs.job: Push supplier payment terms longer as trust grows
jobs.why: Paying the factory months before the stock sells locks up cash. Longer terms let sales pay for the stock.

watch.metric: days between paying the supplier and selling the units, quarterly
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain and Shopify sales

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 100% paid before shipping, 140 days cash tied up. After: 30% deposit and balance on arrival, 95 days.

jobs.job: Catch carrier overbilling
jobs.why: Carriers bill surcharges and weight changes after the fact. Small overcharges on every parcel add up over a year.

watch.metric: carrier invoice amount versus expected charge from shipped weight, monthly
watch.source: carrier invoices joined to Shopify fulfilment events and the shipping app (ShipStation, AfterShip)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: invoices never checked. After: $1,300 a month in wrong surcharges found and disputed.

jobs.job: Pay only for stock that actually arrived
jobs.why: Paying the invoice without checking what arrived means paying for short or wrong shipments.

watch.metric: purchase orders where the invoice, the order and the goods received do not match, count and value, monthly
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain and Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: invoices paid on receipt. After: 2 short shipments worth $3,400 caught and credited this quarter.

jobs.job: Choose sea or air freight so stock lands on time at the lowest cost
jobs.why: Air freight saves weeks but can cost 5 times more. Rushing by air because of late planning eats margin.

watch.metric: freight cost per unit, and shipments landing by the planned date
watch.source: supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain and freight forwarder invoices

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40% of units flown because orders were late. After: earlier orders and sea freight bring air to 10%.

jobs.job: Watch raw material costs behind the main products
jobs.why: When cotton or other inputs fall, the supplier rarely lowers the price on their own. When they rise, a price increase follows.

watch.metric: input cost index versus the price when the product cost was last agreed, monthly
watch.source: public commodity price source logged in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: cotton down 15% since the last price lock, no ask made. After: a cost-down asked and 4% agreed.

jobs.job: Make stock counts match what is on the shelf
jobs.why: If the system says 200 and the shelf has 150, the store oversells and the reorder math is wrong.

watch.metric: counted units versus system units, per cycle count
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6% gap between system and shelf on top products. After: monthly counts bring it under 1%.
